Caesars Unveils "Olympus," a New $1.5 Million Loyalty Tier

Published August 26, 2026 · 4 min read · By the OddsLighthouse Editorial Team

Caesars Entertainment has introduced a new top-of-pyramid loyalty tier called Olympus, sitting above the long-standing Seven Stars level and requiring roughly $1.5 million in theoretical spending to unlock — making it the most expensive publicly disclosed casino loyalty tier in the US market. The tier launches in January 2027, with founding members notified the following month.

What it takes to qualify

Olympus requires 300,000 tier credits, double the threshold of Seven Stars, Caesars Rewards' previous top level. Credits can come from gaming play, hotel stays, dining, entertainment, sportsbook wagering, and online casino activity across the Caesars Rewards network, which spans more than 65 million members and 54 North American properties. Reaching the credit threshold alone doesn't guarantee entry, though — Caesars says membership also requires an explicit invitation from the company, a structure the operator says is meant to keep the tier genuinely exclusive rather than automatic.

What members get

Olympus members earn tier credits 40% faster than standard rates, and benefits include complimentary suite upgrades subject to availability, invitation-only VIP event access, and an annual seven-night stay at a Caesars destination. A dedicated physical Olympus card is set to launch February 1, 2027, and the company is planning an inaugural "Founders Party" at Caesars Palace in March 2027 for the tier's first cohort of members.

Why it matters

The launch is a visible bet on the high-roller segment at a moment when Caesars' Las Vegas Strip revenue has come under pressure, and it arrives as the company is also navigating a reported takeover approach from Tilman Fertitta's Fertitta Entertainment. Competitors including MGM's Noir and Wynn's Chairman's Club maintain comparable invitation-only top tiers, but keep their qualification thresholds private — Caesars' decision to publish a specific dollar figure is a departure from how rivals typically handle their most exclusive rewards levels, and it signals how aggressively operators are now competing for a shrinking pool of the highest-spending players.

A loyalty tier requiring roughly $1.5 million in spending is aimed at an extremely small slice of players. If gambling ever stops feeling like entertainment regardless of stakes, see our responsible gambling resources.
